conclusion: Literal -prod retires fewer instructions in every pair. Unprofiled wall timings are mixed; smooth 60 fps remains open.

build.parallel: V -prod -parallel-cc -prealloc -gc none; actual 33-unit plan, per-unit V -O2/-O3 defaults, no LTO
build.driver: tools/compare_prod_modes.py; actual V generations, preprocessed and sealed before optimizing C

protocol_details.cache: Fresh empty private profile/cache for every trial; OS filesystem/shader caches retained
protocol_details.network: 42 frozen original-origin responses, including self-compilation.mp4; SOCKS replay, private TLS trust, no network forwarding
protocol_details.gpu: Default enabled setting; actual GPU draws verified separately during input for both modes
protocol_details.endpoint: Changed native layer publications after updateLayer; not physical display scanout
protocol_details.counters: Main browser process, all threads, first wheel dispatch through completion of both last dispatch and its first publication; excludes startup, settling, child processes, GPU execution and outside services

limitations: CPU and instruction totals are over 600 inputs, but painting coalesces input: median moving publications are 534 single and 496 parallel. Per-publication values normalize all main-process work, including animation/video/background work; they are not isolated render costs.

Counter trials are separately instrumented. Unprofiled timings use two alternating pairs and show one gain and one regression. They do not establish a repeatable wall-time speedup or physical displayed fps.

All seven paired totals favor single-unit instructions, but the median percentage is descriptive, not a conservative 10-percent site acceptance gate. This is a compiler-mode comparison, with no Brave cohort.

Shared native publications changed the renderer after source sealing. Both variants were rebuilt against a common renderer; another publication before the final cohort installed the newer common renderer recorded in protocol.runtime_inputs. The final cohort pins that same renderer for both V executable variants and verifies GPU/CPU parity. It compares V main executable modes inside one canonical production bundle, not independently rebuilt whole bundles.

The legacy raw summary cpu_ms and user_ns/system_ns labels are incorrect: their CPU fields contain Mach ticks. Corrected measured/medians fields apply the independently calibrated 125/3 ns factor; raw files are retained unchanged. The reader was fixed and its native regression test now compares against CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID.

Source sealing rejected the first two attempts; the third stopped after single compilation because the V driver removed its temporary cwd. Resume was rejected after a native-library change. A relink completed both modes. The first browser diagnostic controller rejected a buffered-log parsing mistake although GPU work and pixel error 3 were present. Every failure and restoration receipt is retained.
One independent 0.2-CPU-second clock calibration overlapped the counter cohort. Other host work continued; the 18-core host one-minute load ranged from 6.37 to 13.25.

final_guard.metric: sampled sum of process-tree RSS; shared pages may be counted twice
